title: The server sums a period's spend per person, agent, model and account, so Home and the canvas draw totals they never add up themselves
purpose: The 18 October 2026 surface review's dashboard domain (builder 06, lys-review/CONSENSUS.md, Server asks) found that Home's cost-this-week figure is added up in the page from each agent's own numbers (surface/identity/src/features/dashboard/Spend.tsx weekTotal), as the canvas does again in its own way (surface/identity/src/features/runtime/canvas-widgets.ts, lines 106 to 125 at ca1228b0), so the two disagree when one agent's read is refused or one record has no price, and neither can say a per-person figure, which a small owner (rung 2 of lys-review/STAKEHOLDERS-2026-10-18.md) needs and GET /dashboard, own agents only, cannot give. The server already sums usage per holder in crates/lys-identity-server/src/budgets_totals.rs.
task: Add GET /usage/summary?period=day|week|month&by=person,agent,model,account to lys-identity-server, answering the period's spend in US dollars (micros), tokens and running time per person, per agent, per model and per account, each row the server's own sum, with a total and, for each, how many records gave no price, a refused part answered as {refusal, reason} in place of its rows, never a zero. Home's Spend and the canvas's widgets draw that answer and add nothing.

requirements.title: GET /usage/summary answers the period's sums per person, agent, model and account
requirements.spec: Behavioural. GET /usage/summary?period=day|week|month&by=person,agent,model,account answers, for the signed-in caller and over what the caller may read, { period, since_ms, zone, total: { dollars_micros, tokens, running_ms, unpriced_records }, by: { person | agent | model | account: [{ id, name, dollars_micros, tokens, running_ms, unpriced_records }] } }, each row summed by the server from the same records crates/lys-identity-server/src/budgets_totals.rs sums today; by lists only the groupings asked for; a grouping the caller may not read in full is answered as { refusal, reason } in place of its rows; a record with no price counts in unpriced_records and adds nothing to dollars_micros. The route is a row in openapi_table.rs. No fixed period boundary is assumed from the server's clock alone: since_ms and zone are those the caller's /me says, as /dashboard does today.
acceptance: Red first: a test in crates/lys-identity-server/src/usage_summary_tests.rs seeds three agents of two people with priced and unpriced records across two models and reads the four groupings, the total, and unpriced_records equal to the unpriced count; a caller who may read only their own agents reads the person grouping as a refusal and their own agents' rows
The openapi contract test is green with the route

requirements.title: Home and the canvas draw the server's sums and add nothing
requirements.spec: Behavioural. surface/identity/src/features/dashboard/Spend.tsx reads GET /usage/summary?period=week&by=person,agent and draws its total and rows as returned; weekTotal and every addition in the page go. surface/identity/src/features/runtime/canvas-widgets.ts reads the same route and draws it; its own sums (lines 106 to 125 at ca1228b0) go, and its "(n of m reporting)" becomes "from n of m agents in full", n being the agents with unpriced_records 0. A refused grouping is one line saying what could not be read, never a zero. Money through the one formatter (shell/count.ts money).
acceptance: Spend's and the canvas's vitest cases feed one summary answer with a refused grouping and an unpriced record and show the server's figures, the refusal line, and "from 2 of 3 agents in full"; grep of Spend.tsx and canvas-widgets.ts for reduce( over dollars answers 0

boundaries: SHALL NOT answer a zero for a part that could not be read: a refusal is named in place.
SHALL NOT sum anything in the surface.
SHALL NOT put a fixed wait, deadline or poll anywhere, in code or test.
verification: Red first for every requirement; cargo nextest run only (never cargo test), clippy pedantic -D warnings, cargo fmt; vitest and tsc for the surface files; the design gate's validate.py and check-coverage.py on the cluster parsed for FAIL lines, never by exit code; file length 500 on every file touched.

Done means: every route and field answers as specified with the named tests green on the Mac, the surface reads each one, the openapi contract test is green, and the lane's END names any file it touched beyond the lists here so the brief is amended in one commit.
